Tier 3. Owns the boundary between the core and the profiles, the
declared-binding rule and the import rule that every profile applies
(§1), and indexes the profiles (§2 to §6). A profile is a domain or
operational specialisation of the method; the members of tiers 1 and 2
are the core.

## 1. The boundary

The core names no runtime, no carrier and no executor. Terms owned outside
the core, by a profile, a realisation or an rc.2 member, never enter tier
1 or 2 except in a disposition table: graph, edge, vector, ledger, event
log, worksite, HoG, Markov overlay, screen, entity cut, and the design
profile's IACS and Prime. The traversal record and the functor kinds F_D,
F_P and F_H are tier-1 calculus terms owned by AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §5, and
"module" is a generic term, as the predecessor's generic testing law uses
it; neither is restricted here. A profile may bind a core mechanism to one of these;
the binding is declared in the profile with its direction, preserved
meaning, narrowed scope and invalidation. In this member "binding" means
that declared binding of a core mechanism; a Product's adoption binding is
[PRODUCT_DEFINITION §7](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#7-collective-reference-frame-basis)'s,
and a carrier binding to a typed contract is [UX §7](UX.md#7-carrier-binding)'s;
the three are not interchanged. The declared-binding rule is new
(P0 boundary, P1); its shape follows ODD's specialisations of F_P and F_H,
which [ODD §5 Probabilistic compute](ODD.md#probabilistic-compute) owns in
the graph-native context and carries as their provenance; the
predecessor's section is rc.2
[ODD probabilistic compute](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/ODD_METHOD.md#probabilistic-compute).

Import rule. A profile imports the generic families of tiers 1 and 2 that
its rules rest on, and owns only its own bindings: the terms and choices
it adds for its domain or operation, among them the declared bindings
above (P1, P6). It imports each concept it uses from a member of tiers 1
and 2 under
[FOUNDATIONS §2 Imports between members](FOUNDATIONS.md#imports-between-members),
which states what an import is, and restates none of that member's rules.
Its family table, in the format of
[FOUNDATIONS §3 Foundation to law](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundation-to-law),
names each imported family by its ID and the section that holds its table,
in the premise column; the profile's rules rest on that family's
consequences, with the standing FOUNDATIONS §3 gives them, and the
family's rules and choices keep their owners. A profile that refines
another profile declares the refinement in its lead; the refined profile
keeps its rules, and the refining profile owns only what it adds (P1, P6).
The import rule is new in this corpus. Purpose and material relation:
each profile table cites the families it rests on without restating them,
so no generic rule gains a second owner in a profile and no choice a
profile adds is presented as following from the foundations (P6, P1).

A worked application, a hello world or a data mapper is an external test
subject; its particulars cannot become generic method functionality by
precedent.

## 2. Graph execution

Graph execution is two tier-3 members, indexed here; each restates its
predecessor in full in its own text and declares its bindings under §1
(P0 boundary, P1):

| Member | Receives | Binds or adds |
|---|---|---|
| [ODD](ODD.md) | rc.2 ODD_METHOD, all 48 rows | the bounded step of FOUNDATIONS P0 to one vector or edge traversal and the graph-native F_P, F_D and F_H shorthands, with F_P and F_H as declared specialisations of SPEC_METHOD §5 ([§5 Probabilistic compute](ODD.md#probabilistic-compute)); the refinement of ACTIVATION §4 to graph functions, with the cumulative environment law of §11.8 declared as its specialised contract for carrying earlier outputs ([§5 Graph functions](ODD.md#graph-functions), [§11.8](ODD.md#118-cumulative-environment-law-is-mandatory)) |
| [TRAVERSAL_OCCURRENCE](TRAVERSAL_OCCURRENCE.md) | rc.2 TRAVERSAL_OCCURRENCE_PROFILE, all 26 rows, 25 conserved and 1 proposed superseded, pending the product owner | an optional closed model-family signature over one exact `a_c` basis of AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS for immutable occurrence histories over a mutable subject, with OP-001 to OP-007 |

The ownership split of graph execution (runtime, product, service layers)
is [ODD §10](ODD.md#10-what-an-odd-product-is); the worker's internal
solution strategy stays outside the framework under
[ODD §5](ODD.md#probabilistic-compute). Where another member says that
this section keeps the ODD binding, the binding is the one ODD states and
this section indexes (P0, P1).

## 3. Software design

[DESIGN_MODULE](DESIGN_MODULE.md) is the software-design profile. It
imports the core and binds: ontology-first derivation of operation
identities from discovered functionality through logical completeness,
Prime contraction, the irreducible architectural carrier set and its
projections; proportional design sequencing with the decision-complete
design gate; bounded frame conservation; native constructability;
capability and foundation selection; transformation admission
completeness; invariant reconstruction sufficiency; computational
realisation projection; the module taxonomy and realisation rules; and
the design review questions and checklist. Its design-to-module evidence
route, module-derived unit tests and module lifecycle confirmation are
ASSURANCE §14 to §16, and its core rule and non-goals SPEC_METHOD §2
Realisation shape. The per-boundary cost of the derivation chain is
decided there (DESIGN_MODULE §5 Proportional design sequencing, §7 Gate
and retrospective work) (P2, P0).

## 4. UX

[UX](UX.md) is the UX profile. It refines DESIGN_MODULE for modules that
realise a UX surface, imports the core, and binds: the Elm process model
with typed State, Msg, Update, View, Cmd and Sub; the boundary between UX
messages and admitted product carriers; the state transition law; the
effect membrane; binding to AssetSurface or an equivalent typed contract;
view continuation and the Msg-replay proof; view shape; type sharing with
runtime validation at untrusted seams; the accessibility minimum;
realisation discretion; adoption with the scaffold and exemption law and
UX sprint compliance escrow; the failure patterns and review questions;
and its refinements of the core result algebra, each value mapped to one
core value (UX §15). Its binding of TICKETS §3's generalised escrow terms
is declared in its lead (P6, P2).

## 5. World model

[WORLD_MODEL](WORLD_MODEL.md) is the world-model profile. It imports the
core and binds: the imported product-lineage concepts and the Builder
Project specialisation; the Markov-object construct at candidate status
with its effective blanket, working refinements, epistemic status and
promotion gate; the core claims and units; entity recovery and the entity
cut as the published identity-bearing unit, with its admissibility,
discrimination and publication law; the attribute ledger; the
representation, materialisation and publication laws; Markov-object
overlay construction; saturation; composition of local artifacts;
projection; the control and data planes; the proof law and
world-model-driven development; and its refinements of the core result
algebra, each value mapped to one core value (WORLD_MODEL §14). Its
binding of FOUNDATIONS §2 Object
and P3's boundary claim to the entity cut is declared in its lead.
Nothing in the core depends on the construct being established (P3, P6).

## 6. Engagement baseline

[EXECUTIVE_BASELINE](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md) is the optional
engagement-baseline profile. It imports the core and describes the
executive configuration, one configuration in the sense of
[ACTIVATION §1 Configuration](ACTIVATION.md#configuration), with three
engagement frames (Executive, Worker, Reviewer) and a catalogue of
specialist frames, mapped onto the law of tiers 1 and 2. Its frame names
bind the responsibilities that configuration allocates under
[ACTIVATION §1 Roles and delegation](ACTIVATION.md#roles-and-delegation),
not roles imported by spelling, as its lead declares (P1, P6).

## 7. Source dispositions

Each cell names where the rows of one rc.2 member receive their
dispositions. Every row's disposition is one of the four values of
[RELEASE §9](RELEASE.md#9-successor-baseline-conservation-stdo-up-015); a
row with none is unresolved, which blocks qualification of the claim it
affects.

| rc.2 member | Disposition |
|---|---|
| ODD_METHOD | conserved in full in ODD (all 48 rows; its §21), indexed in §2; the generic parts (bounded unit, refinement, loop structure) are generalised into ACTIVATION; the declared-binding rule of §1 is new |
| TRAVERSAL_OCCURRENCE_PROFILE | 25 rows conserved and 1 proposed superseded, pending the product owner, disposed in TRAVERSAL_OCCURRENCE, Source dispositions; indexed in §2 |
| baseline runtime bindings | disposed row by row in EXECUTIVE_BASELINE, with STDO_REFERENCE_FRAME_BASELINE; §6 is its index entry |

| UX_METHOD | disposed row by row in UX; §4 is its index entry. The first-pass description of UX by reader and task obligations, operational projection and screen-level acceptance was candidate text with no source in UX_METHOD, so it is no predecessor claim; it is withdrawn |

{"status":"ok","path":"standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","anchor":"","start_line":2391,"end_line":2435,"total_lines":2594,"content":"## 12. Adoption and relations

### Adoption

Who may adopt this profile is stated once in
[PRODUCT_DEFINITION §7](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#7-collective-reference-frame-basis):
inclusion in the selected method cut makes the profile available, and only
Product authority adopts it. This profile adds no adopter. The adopting
Product's authority may record its adoption by citing the profile in ADRs
or design surfaces; naming it in the project's agent entry surface (such
as `AGENTS.md`) as the preferred realisation discipline; using it as
review criteria for implementation-migration tickets; and classifying
implementation modules by the taxonomy of §9 (P2, P6;
rc.2 #15-adoption-guidance).

When the profile is adopted, the project applies it consistently across the
named boundary: Ontology and architecture derivation; design modules;
runtime or execution kernels; prompt assembly and reporting paths;
constructors and materialisers; and projection and query surfaces. For
migrations involving carrier closure, schema closure or governance
boundaries, projects should make the boundary closure evaluators (§3)
explicit in the governing ADR or ticket rather than leaving them implicit
(P6).

Every new or materially changed adopted semantic boundary declares or
cites its accepted Ontology before claiming design-method completion. The
Ontology evidence includes entity lifecycle, authority, function
derivation, whole-family Prime, each accepted atom's admitted domain,
atom-to-realisation projection mappings and projection traceability, at
the granularity applicable to the material change (P6, P2). When the
material change includes schema or typed carrier work, the project derives
and reconciles the IACS from that Ontology before claiming design-method
completion. When the new or materially changed boundary is derived from an
existing realisation, the project also publishes the reference-to-target
derivation asset and the Ontology-derived three-view design asset before
claiming design-method completion for the changed boundary. When the new or
materially changed boundary has active implementation, the project also
publishes a module-derived unit test lane (ASSURANCE §15) before claiming
closure for that change (P6).

Partial adoption is allowed, but the adopted boundary and adopted rule
family should be named explicitly. Partial adoption may narrow scope; it is
not used to claim design-method completion while skipping the evidence
needed to audit, refactor or reconstruct the realised boundary (P6, P2).

{"status":"ok","path":"standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","anchor":"","start_line":1536,"end_line":1608,"total_lines":2594,"content":"### Gate and retrospective work

For a new or semantically changed boundary, the Ontology and design
verdict are both `accepted` before the affected implementation, public
contract or semantic carrier is promoted or the work claims design-method
closure. Any failed applicable axiom, missing functionality disposition,
unresolved authority path or blocking realisation gap keeps the verdict
non-accepted (P6; rc.2 #gate-and-retrospective-work).

The Ontology verdict and the design verdict are each an acceptance
result: a decision that consumes the results of assessment, distinct from
them. The decision owner is the
design authority that accepts the Ontology (§5), and the verdict is its
disposition of the Ontology or of the design pack at the design gate,
under [ACTIVATION §3 Disposition](ACTIVATION.md#disposition), which owns
the dispositions and their core values. `accepted` is the disposition
`accept`, which maps to `satisfied` for "the candidate is accepted at its
declared boundary", the candidate being the Ontology or the design pack
and the boundary the design gate. A verdict that is not `accepted` is one
of the other three dispositions, mapped there, or no disposition yet,
which is no acceptance result. The verdict consumes the pack's availability
and assessment results, among them the evaluation of decision
completeness, which is the design gate's acceptance criterion
([§5 Decision-complete symbolic design](#decision-complete-symbolic-design)),
the axiom verdicts and the cross-view proofs, and stays separate from both
(FOUNDATIONS §4 Results, availability, assessment and acceptance): a matrix in which every applicable axiom is
`pass` is evidence for the design authority, never the verdict, and a
step that produced the pack establishes neither. An axiom whose result
is not `satisfied`, whether `fail` or a core value recorded directly, an
applicable axiom with no result, or an axiom with no result whose
applicability is not established false, keeps the verdict non-accepted
as a failed axiom does, because a combination with a non-satisfied
mandatory result or a gap is never `satisfied`
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results))
(P6, P5). The binding to ACTIVATION §3 is new in this corpus. Purpose and
material relation: neither a passing matrix nor a produced design pack is
read as acceptance, and the design gate's acceptance combines with other
results in the one core (P6).

For an unchanged `realization_refactor`, the gate is proportional: cite
the accepted Ontology and design basis, identify the touched projection
set, and prove that entities, relationships, lifecycle, authority,
functions, effects and public semantics have no delta. That proof reuses
the existing verdict; it does not create a new Ontology or acceptance
ceremony (P2; ACTIVATION §7).

When `co_evolution_admissible(B)` holds, implementation may precede or
develop with design evidence and may be retained after reconciliation.
Until the design gate is accepted it is provisional evidence: it does not
author semantic truth, earn publication authority, or satisfy promotion or
closure. Otherwise only a disposable spike may cross the affected
unresolved, contradictory or materially non-equivalent relation before
design acceptance (P6, P2).

Existing implementation placed under retrospective review may continue to
inform the affected design. Co-evolution remains lawful only while
`co_evolution_admissible(B)` holds; newly discovered material ambiguity,
contradiction or a materially non-equivalent network makes
`decision_complete(B)` false and activates the design gate for that
decision. Promotion and design-method closure remain blocked until the
required Ontology, three-view asset and axiom evaluation are accepted. The
design evaluates the code against prior authority; it does not rewrite the
Ontology or diagrams merely to rationalise an unlawful implementation
shape (P6).

The asset stays boundary-bounded. It is a defect if it mixes an active
semantic boundary with unrelated bootstrap, test-harness, projection or
delivery shapes merely to look complete (P2). If the Ontology, any of the
three views, the cross-view evaluation or either accepted verdict is
absent, the boundary is not design-method complete. Work may continue as
provisional co-evolution only when `co_evolution_admissible(B)` holds, but
the affected boundary may not be promoted, published or closed (P6).

{"status":"ok","path":"standards/ACTIVATION.md","anchor":"","start_line":943,"end_line":1171,"total_lines":1838,"content":"## 3. Step results and disposition

A step returns its results in the core algebra of
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results): each evaluation it
performed returns one core value with its predicate and domain outcome,
and an evaluation it did not perform has no result. The outcomes of
admitting and activating a step, and the step's own outcomes, answer other
questions than its evaluations do. This section owns them as five
refinements of the core. Each names the question it answers and the
predicate its mapping is for, and maps each of its values to exactly one
core value; the predicate travels with the value, so no refinement's
`satisfied` counts toward another predicate
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results)).
Purpose and material relation: admission, work, decisions and effects
stand in the one core (P5, P6), so a consumer that combines them cannot
read a refused activation as a step's stop, availability as fitness or
acceptance, a carried ambiguity as resolved, or an unknown effect as none.

| Refinement | Question | Predicate of the mapping |
|---|---|---|
| admission and activation | may the step begin | the step is lawfully admitted and activated on the exact subject and basis |
| construction availability | did the step yield its output | a candidate is available |
| disposition | what the decision owner does with an assessed candidate | the candidate is accepted at its declared boundary |
| ambiguity outcome | what happened to a declared ambiguity | the declared ambiguity is resolved on the exact basis |
| effects | did an intended external effect occur | the intended effect occurred |

A profile that refines these values for its own units maps each of its
values to exactly one core value under FOUNDATIONS §4 Results and adds no
core value.

### Admission and activation

A step exists only after its contract is admitted (§1, Admission) and its
frame is activated on the exact subject and basis (§2). The outcomes of
admission and of context construction are owned here; each maps for the
predicate "the step is lawfully admitted and activated on the exact
subject and basis", and its cause selects its value (P5, P6; RF-005 for
the basis causes). The outcomes of frame activation are the `activate`
refinement of [REFERENCE_FRAME §5](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#5-method-functions),
which owns their causes, their predicate and their core values. Because
this predicate requires activation, a refused activation decides it with
the value REFERENCE_FRAME §5 gives; the table names those outcomes and
maps none of them again:

| Outcome | Cause | Core value |
|---|---|---|
| `activated` | the contract is admitted with its admission evidence (§1), Z, R, the required-edge semantics, the basis and the scope are exact and the material closure is finite and unique (§2, step 1), its projection returns a selected context (§2, step 2), and activation returns `activated_frame` | satisfied |
| `admission_refused(authority)` | the work authority the step needs is not admitted: no admission mechanism or explicit human override admits the exact contract, or no durable result and evidence surface is authorised and available; the outcome names the missing authority or surface and its owner | out_of_frame |
| `admission_refused(basis)` | the contract's cited outcome, prerequisite or experiment basis, or the exact subject and basis it names, cannot support it; the outcome names that basis | invalid_basis |
| `closure_unresolved` | the seed set Z, the relation family R, the required-edge semantics, the basis or the scope is not exact, or the material closure is not finite and unique on the exact basis (§2, step 1; AC-010), or the projection of the closure returns a gap or refusal (§2, step 2; AC-011); the outcome names the condition that fails and the basis coordinates that leave it open | invalid_basis |
| `out_of_frame` | no available frame and actor pairing declares a material relation or capability the evaluation needs (§2, Activation), or no fit option of §2 step 3 fits the selected context to an actor's envelope | out_of_frame |
| `activation_refusal` with its cause | a cause REFERENCE_FRAME §5 states | the core value REFERENCE_FRAME §5 maps that cause to |

These outcomes are not values of construction availability and are not
results of a step. A refused admission or activation creates no step, no
activation of the step's frame and no work result, the closed output of a
constructing actor to its consumer; the outcome returns to the assigning
authority or the declared result carrier, and no consumer records it as a
step's stop state. [EXECUTIVE_BASELINE §5](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md#work-result)
applies this rule to the Worker (provenance
[work result](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/STDO_REFERENCE_FRAME_BASELINE.md#work-result)).
Purpose and material relation: a mismatch known before the step begins is
reported with its cause in the one core, so it is neither mistaken for a
step that stopped nor for one that ran.

### Construction availability

A step's output is a candidate until evaluated (FOUNDATIONS §3, P0): the
constructed subject of a constructing step, or the closed results of an
assessing step. Construction availability records whether that output
exists (P5, P6; provenance
[work result](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/STDO_REFERENCE_FRAME_BASELINE.md#work-result)):

| Value | Core value | Ground |
|---|---|---|
| `candidate_ready` | satisfied | an exact candidate and its transition evidence are available |
| `refused` | falsified | lawful activation occurred, and a governing prohibition or an owner-valid construction refusal defeats the requested construction; the prohibition or refusal is the counterexample |
| `incomplete` | falsified | the lawfully activated step stopped without its output, because an evaluation the output needs was not performed or could not be decided on the admissible evidence, or bounded execution ended first; the stop basis is the counterexample, and it and the residuals name which |

The mapping is total and exclusive after lawful activation: the cause of
the stop selects the value, and payload wording, stop timing or actor
preference cannot select another. A mismatch known during admission or
activation is no value of this refinement, because no step exists; it
takes its outcome under Admission and activation above.

`satisfied` here establishes availability only and never counts toward the
candidate's fitness or acceptance (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results).

to `indeterminate`. The step's evaluations keep their own results: each
evaluation it performed returns its core value, `indeterminate` where the
admissible evidence could not decide; each evaluation it planned and did
not perform has no result, and its work state (§5) carries it as a
residual with the capability or the execution left unfinished

not performed thus stays distinct from one whose evidence cannot decide

availability concerns its own output, never the subject under assessment

because a decision cannot be taken on a basis that cannot support it (P5,

### Disposition

The decision owner disposes an assessed candidate with one of four
semantic dispositions (§1, Roles and delegation; P6, P5; provenance rc.2
SPEC_METHOD #proportional-disposition). An assessor may recommend one; the
recommendation is evidence for the decision owner, never a disposition
([EVALUATION §4](EVALUATION.md#4-review-results)). The disposition is the
acceptance result: it consumes the candidate's availability and assessment
results and stays separate from both (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results). Each maps
to the core for the predicate "the candidate is accepted at its declared
boundary":

| Disposition | Condition | Core value |
|---|---|---|
| `accept` | the candidate closes its declared cone and preserves every affected governing relation | satisfied |
| `local_repair` | implementation or proof is locally defective while the governing relation remains coherent | falsified |
| `re_enter` | the governing outcome, a requirement, an identity, a lifecycle, an authority, a public contract or the accepted design must change | invalid_basis |
| `reject` | the candidate violates a governing relation or leaves an undisposed competing truth path | falsified |

For `local_repair` the local defect, and for `reject` the violated relation
or the competing truth path, is the counterexample to accepting this
candidate; a repaired candidate is a new candidate with its own results.
For `re_enter` the governing basis the candidate was built and assessed on
must change, so that basis cannot support acceptance; the change re-enters
at its owning relation (§4). The core values are new; they place
acceptance in the one core, as FOUNDATIONS §4 Results requires, so that a
consumer combining results cannot take availability or assessment as
acceptance (P6).

Global correctness means conserving every global relation affected by the
bounded action; it does not require proving the whole product inside every
local action (P4b). Repeated rejection against one unchanged boundary
requires reassessment of the frame altitude, the causal cone, the common
components, the design-versus-code placement and the authority
sufficiency. The method sets no rejection-count threshold, mandatory
review-round count or review state machine; it prohibits repeating an
unchanged failed construction relation as if iteration alone could close
it (P2).

### Ambiguity outcome

A declared ambiguity is resolved, carried, escalated or blocked, and the
outcome is recorded either way (§4, which also names the hard stops;
[SPEC_METHOD §5](SPEC_METHOD.md#5-ambiguity-governance-and-lifecycle)
applies this to the method's chain of authority surfaces). Each outcome
maps to the core for the predicate "the declared ambiguity is resolved on
the exact basis" (P5, P6):

| Outcome | Core value | Ground |
|---|---|---|
| `resolved` | satisfied | a decision was taken under the policy that permits lawful probabilistic processing, or by human adjudication, and recorded |
| `carried` | falsified | policy permits work to continue with the ambiguity open; the open ambiguity is the counterexample, and it stays a recorded residual that names the evidence or decision that would resolve it |
| `escalated` | out_of_frame | policy or risk appetite reserves the decision to human adjudication, an authority the step does not hold; the value names that authority |
| `blocked` | falsified | the ambiguity stays unresolved, and policy or a hard stop (§4) halts work at it; the open ambiguity is the counterexample, and the value names the halting condition and what would lift it |

An open ambiguity is a known state of the exact basis, so `carried` and
`blocked` decide the predicate false; neither is `indeterminate`, whose
evidence cannot decide the predicate. Each keeps its domain outcome with
the value: `carried` with what would resolve the ambiguity, `blocked` with
the halting condition and what would lift it (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results,
Recording). No outcome other than `resolved` maps to `satisfied`, so a
dependent claim cannot rest on a carried, escalated or blocked ambiguity
as if it were resolved. The mapping is new; it places ambiguity outcomes
in the one core, which FOUNDATIONS §4 Results requires of every outcome
(P5, P6).

### Effects

An effectful step's intended external effect has one of three values,
mapped for the predicate "the intended effect occurred", that is, the
declared outcome of the effect is attained. The value turns on what the
admitted evidence establishes about that outcome (P5 with the open-world
premise, P6):

| Value | Core value | Ground |
|---|---|---|
| `completed` | satisfied | evidence about the subject establishes that the intended effect occurred in full and that the effect has ended |
| `not_effected` | falsified | evidence about the subject establishes that the declared outcome is not attained and that no later completion of the effect can attain it, for example where no effect began, the effect ended short, an interval that the declared outcome bounds has closed with part of it not done, or the part already done has itself made the declared outcome unattainable, as when it destroyed what the outcome needed; any part that did occur is named with the value |
| `completion_unknown` | indeterminate | neither of the other values is established: the evidence cannot decide whether the intended effect has occurred or will occur, as for a request whose response was lost with no counterexample observed; or the evidence shows the intended effect in full while the effect may still be acting, and the outcome stays undecided until what the effect leaves on the subject is settled; its residual names the observation that would decide |

`not_effected` requires evidence about the subject. A lost response, an
absent record, or an actor's context that holds no trace of the effect is
not that evidence, and the value stays `completion_unknown`.
`completion_unknown` never maps to `completed` or to `not_effected`.

Whether the effect has ended is a second question beside the predicate
above, and it enters the value only as a conjunct of `completed`. An
effect has ended where evidence about the subject establishes
that it no longer acts on the subject or that it never began. Where an
effect began and the evidence does not establish its end, the end is not
established, and that is recorded beside the value as a residual naming
the observation that would establish it. The end never decides a
`not_effected` value and is never folded into one: when an interval that
the declared outcome bounds has closed with part not done, the value is
`not_effected` while the effect may still be acting. The residual does
not weaken the counterexample, and the counterexample does not resolve
the residual. `completed` alone requires the end established, so a
counterexample stands without proof that the effect has ended, while
success is never claimed for an effect that may still be acting
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), Standing).

An effect of uncertain completion is one whose value is
`completion_unknown`, or whose value is `not_effected` with its end not
established. §5 reconciles it, sufficiently for the next dependent
action, before any repetition or dependent action. A `not_effected`
value licenses neither treating the effect as absent nor repeating it
while its end is not established.

The refinement is new. Its material relation is whether an action whose
external effect may have occurred is repeated or relied on; §4 names a
lost post-effect response as a case that no added core value solves, and
this refinement records it in the existing core. Keeping the end of the
effect beside the value keeps two facts that one value would merge: a
counterexample already established for the declared outcome, and an
effect that may still be acting.

## 1. Verification layers

Each layer of the chain ([SPEC_METHOD §2 Constitutional chain](SPEC_METHOD.md#constitutional-chain)) preserves a distinct kind of truth

| Layer | What it preserves | Primary question answered |
|---|---|---|
| Requirements | invariant truth | what must be true? |
| Design | structural choice | how is that truth realised? |
| Scenarios | operational meaning | can the realised system actually do the claimed thing? |

Without scenarios a capability can appear covered because the words exist
in requirements and design. Scenarios force the sharper question: can the
product really do the thing? A requirement can name a reusable composable
unit and a design record can describe the types that realise it, but only
a scenario asks whether a user can build such a unit and apply it twice
(P6).

Scenarios are the product-owner layer: concrete, end-to-end use cases that
validate the chain from intent to realised behaviour. When a scenario
cannot be written, the capability is not yet real. When a scenario fails,
the gap is between the system's actual behaviour and its claimed
capability, not between the specification's words and its other words (P2,
P6).

Scenarios do not replace requirement categories. They primarily validate
capability claims and other behaviour with concrete operational meaning.
Constraints, governance rules and verification-infrastructure requirements
may require different evidence in addition to, or instead of, end-to-end
scenarios (P2).

{"status":"ok","path":"standards/ACTIVATION.md","anchor":"","start_line":1692,"end_line":1759,"total_lines":1838,"content":"## 7. Closed result and reuse

A closed result identifies the frame and its activation, the subject, the
basis, the evaluation, the actor, the evidence, the verdict, the residual
uncertainty and the invalidation conditions (the minimal shape is
REFERENCE_FRAME §13). The frame's internal working context need not be
transferred when the closed result and its provenance are sufficient for
the consuming decision; it may still be attached, for audit or otherwise,
without changing the result. Independent evaluations may share valid
mechanical evidence under the declared independence conditions of
[EVALUATION §3](EVALUATION.md#3-independent-assessment), which owns that
permission (P4b, P0; rc.2 RF #return-a-closed-result).

The selection of affected results after a change and the conditions for
retaining evidence on a new subject are
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Change impact and evidence reuse](FOUNDATIONS.md#change-impact-and-evidence-reuse);
this section applies them to closed results and handoffs, and the three
invalidators below are kinds of change Δ, and a closed result is affected
when its dependencies `D*(t)` meet the impact cover `I(Δ)` (P3, P6).

A closed result is reused by an unchanged consumer that checks exact
applicability; a role, conversation or resumption change alone invalidates
nothing. An invalidator invalidates the affected result before reliance,
even where the subject's own bytes are unchanged, preserving its
predecessor/successor relation and any demonstrably independent surviving
results. Invalidation withdraws the result from direct reliance; whether
its evidence is retained on the new basis is decided by `retain_applicable`
of FOUNDATIONS §4 Change impact and evidence reuse, and the changed
coordinate alone establishes neither that the claim fails nor that it
holds. The invalidators are three:

- a material input change: a change to the result's subject or to an
  input it rests on, including the admissible evidence that bears on its
  predicate; newly acquired or changed admissible evidence is such a
  change when it is material to the result as
  [FOUNDATIONS §2](FOUNDATIONS.md#2-ontology) defines material, that is,
  when it could change the result's value;
- a changed basis: a change to any coordinate of the basis the result
  binds (FOUNDATIONS §2, Basis);
- a declared revising observation: an observation that the result or
  judgment itself names as one that would revise it, once it occurs.

A changed source, task or actor condition is a changed basis where the
basis binds it, and otherwise a material input change; a role change that
alters a required actor condition is such a change, while a role,
conversation or resumption change that alters none of these invalidates
nothing (P3, P6).

Judgment continuity names the basis and the evidence; Return A Closed
Result names inputs and the observation. A member, profile or project
that names a trigger for its own domain, such as a changed projection,
rule or configuration, names it as an instance of one of these three and
states no parallel list (P3, P4b, P6). A reused judgment does not
satisfy a separately required independent judgment; the independent assessor
acquires its own evidence and supplies its own judgment. Conserves
[Return A Closed Result](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#return-a-closed-result),
[judgment continuity](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/TICKET_METHOD.md#recorded-judgment-and-owner-ruling-continuity),
whose "changed material evidence" is the evidence case of the first
invalidator. Purpose and material relation of naming the three kinds once
and of the instance rule: the predecessor stated its invalidators in
several differing lists, so a consumer had to take their union; one list
with named instances gives every consumer the same triggers, and the
material relation is whether a result is relied on after a change that
could alter it (P3, P6). Whether a revision of a frame needs a new
revision coordinate is
[REFERENCE_FRAME §10](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#revision-actions)'s question;
whether a result it touches stays valid is this section's.

{"status":"ok","path":"standards/FOUNDATIONS.md","anchor":"conjunction-of-results","start_line":1008,"end_line":1130,"total_lines":1614,"content":"### Conjunction of results

Conjunction combines results into one result for a composite predicate: a
claim made of component claims, a decision over several evaluations, or
the outer contract of composed steps. It is defined here once, over the
core. A member or profile that combines results applies this rule and
declares only the choices it leaves open (P4a, P4b, P5, P6). Purpose and
material relation: failure, undecidability, non-performance and uncertain
effects stay distinct after combination, so a composite can neither report
success nor hide which kind of gap it has while one of them remains in
what it requires.

A conjunction takes three inputs and keeps them apart:

1. the closed results returned, each a core value with its predicate and
   domain outcome;
2. the planned assessments that have no closed result applicable to the
   composite: evaluations the composite requires that were not performed,
   or whose result is absent, stale, bound to another subject or basis, or
   incapable of establishing its claim;
3. the required coverage that no planned assessment addresses: for a
   required obligation set R and the coverage C that the planned
   assessments admit, the uncovered coverage R minus C.

Gaps. A conjunction with any item in the second or third input is never
`satisfied`. Its record names which kind of gap it has, not performed,
uncovered or both, and each item. An uncovered obligation is never
reported as satisfied or as an omitted planned assessment; a planned
assessment without a closed result is never reported as uncovered or as an
`indeterminate` component.

Stale results. A held result is stale for a composite when the basis it
binds is not the basis the composite requires of that component, because
a later state has superseded or advanced it or because it binds another
subject or basis (§2, Basis). Two questions stay apart, so that one
composite has one reported value (P3, P5, P6):

- an evaluation performed on a subject or basis that is stale, advanced,
  ambiguous or mismatched against the one it must bind returns
  `invalid_basis` for its own predicate, or is reactivated on the current
  basis; [RF-005](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-005-exact-basis-and-coordinates)
  states this law over frames, and a conjunction that receives that
  `invalid_basis` holds it as a returned result;
- a component whose only held result is stale has no closed result
  applicable to the composite: on the basis the composite requires, its
  evaluation was not performed. It is a planned assessment without a
  closed result, in the second input, and a gap. Its stale value is
  neither counted as a returned result nor relabelled `invalid_basis` for
  the composite, and it stays in the record with its own basis;
- the declared basis relations disagree (Reported value below) only among
  returned results, each bound to the basis the composite requires of it,
  whose bases the declared rule requires to agree or to join in a coherent
  composite basis, and which do not.

A stale `satisfied` never counts toward the composite. Purpose and
material relation: answering one stale component as a gap in one place and
as `invalid_basis` in another would give one composite two reported
values; keeping the evaluation's own value apart from the composite's gap
keeps the reported value unique and the stale result visible.

Survival. Every known failure (a `falsified` result with its
counterexample), every planned assessment without a closed result and
every uncovered obligation is carried with the composite and survives every
join: combining conjunctions takes the union of known failures and of
planned assessments without a closed result, and recomputes uncovered
coverage over the combined obligations. A known failure and a gap of
either kind survive every join. Common agreement among contributors
cannot discard a constraint or a material counterexample that only one
contributor found. A missing, wrong-subject, conflicted or indeterminate
mandatory result stays unresolved under the declared rule, and aggregate
satisfied status cannot replace it (P4b, P5).

Predicates travel. Each component keeps its predicate and domain outcome
through every join, so an uncertain effect stays distinct from a failure
and from an undecided claim, and a `satisfied` for one predicate never
counts toward another: a step's `satisfied` for "a candidate is available"
never counts toward the candidate's fitness or acceptance.

Reported value. The conjunction is `satisfied` only when every mandatory
result is `satisfied` with valid applicable evidence, the declared basis
relations agree, and the second and third inputs are empty. A composite
with a material counterexample to a mandatory constraint or an uncovered
required obligation cannot project success. Where a mandatory result is
not `satisfied`, the conjunction
reports a non-satisfied value chosen by its declared rule from those
returned; no universal order among the non-satisfied values exists, and
the member or profile that applies the conjunction declares its own in
its declared rule. Where every mandatory returned result is `satisfied`
and the declared basis relations disagree, the conjunction reports
`invalid_basis`, because no coherent composite basis supports the
composite predicate (§2, Basis); any gaps stay recorded by kind. Where
every mandatory returned result is `satisfied`, the declared basis
relations agree and a gap remains, the conjunction reports
`indeterminate`, because the results it holds cannot decide the composite
predicate; that value is the conjunction's own, and the gaps stay
recorded by kind. A `falsified` result that is not mandatory stays in the
conjunction's record with its predicate and is never discarded. Where
every mandatory result is `satisfied`, the declared basis relations agree
and no gap remains, a material counterexample to a mandatory constraint
falsifies the conjunction whichever contributor found it, and without one
the conjunction's value is the one its declared rule gives over the
mandatory results.

The declared rule. A conjunction declares which results are mandatory; how
conflict and indeterminacy are handled; which basis relations must agree,
results on different bases combining only under a declared coherent
composite basis (§2, Basis); which decision authority owns the
conjunction; how results that are not mandatory count; and whether any
result may veto or defer the decision.
Conjunction does not transfer the semantic authority of a contributing
evaluation (P6, P4a).

Composition of results. The result of composed steps for the outer
predicate is the conjunction of the steps' results, with the outer
contract's obligations as the required coverage. That each step returned
`satisfied` supports the outer predicate only where the refinement's
premises hold ([ACTIVATION §4](ACTIVATION.md#4-totality-and-refinement),
Refinement).

Provenance: rc.2 RF #result-conjunction and
#applicability-and-required-results, and the combination rule of
conservation accounting.

{"status":"ok","path":"standards/FOUNDATIONS.md","anchor":"","start_line":1409,"end_line":1443,"total_lines":1614,"content":"### Change impact and evidence reuse

Assertion justification and evidence validity are related but distinct
dependency relations. The former explains why a check expresses an
obligation. The latter identifies what can affect the check's behaviour,
conclusion or applicability: implementation, shared libraries, data,
